beats: Farmers painted their barns with the ashes of dead stars. And they had no idea.
You'd think barns are red so cows can find their way home. Nope. Cows barely see red.

In the 1800s, store paint was expensive. So farmers mixed their own. Linseed oil, milk, lime... and rust. Rust was everywhere on a farm. Dirt cheap. It may even have kept mold off the wood. So the barns turned red.
But you see, rust is iron. And almost every atom of iron was forged inside a star that exploded before the Sun was born. So every red barn is painted with dead stars. And so is the red in your blood.
